You are an AI pair programmer working  on my existing project called "ML-Preprocessing-Tool".
This app already loads datasets (CSV/Excel) and does basic preprocessing/EDA in a modular way .
🎯 OVERALL GOAL
Upgrade this app to support an industry-level data preprocessing pipeline for tabular datasets, in a way that:
Keeps all existing functionality working (no breaking changes).
Adds missing preprocessing steps only if they are not already implemented.
Organizes the preprocessing steps in a clear, logical order (like a real ML production pipeline).
Teaches the user while they use it:
For every step: show what the step does, why it is needed, and why it comes after the previous step.
The UI should feel like an interactive tutorial + practical tool.
Do not blindly refactor or optimize everything.
Only change code where necessary to add features, improve structure, or cleanly integrate the pipeline.
📂 CONTEXT ABOUT THE APP
App type: Streamlit.
Structure: Modular, index.py as entry point, separate pages/modules for features (e.g., upload, preprocessing, EDA, etc.).
Goal: Let users upload a dataset and perform ML-ready preprocessing.
When you explore the repo:
First, scan the existing modules and understand what is already implemented (upload, missing values, encoding, scaling, etc.).
Then, map my current functionality to the desired pipeline below.
Finally, add missing pieces + improve UX around the pipeline and explanations.
🧠 TARGET PIPELINE (WHAT YOU MUST IMPLEMENT)
Implement / organize the following industry-level preprocessing steps for tabular data, in this order.
If some steps already exist, reuse them and only improve or re-organize the UI.
Data Ingestion & Schema Standardization
Dataset upload (CSV/Excel already exists – reuse).
Show schema: column names, data types, shape.
Enforce consistent datatypes where possible (int/float/str/bool/datetime).
Data Quality Checks
Missing values overview per column (% missing).
Duplicate records count.
Basic range checks for numerical columns (min, max).
Type validation (e.g., numeric columns with text noise).
Show this in a clear “Data Quality” summary panel.
Data Cleaning
Missing Value Handling
Options: drop rows/columns, mean/median/mode imputation, forward/backward fill.
Duplicate Handling
Show duplicates; allow user to remove them.
Inconsistency Fixing
Standardize category labels (e.g., “Male/male/MALE”).
Strip whitespace, fix casing for string columns.
Outlier Processing
Detect outliers using simple IQR method at least.
Show which columns and how many outliers.
Give user options: remove, cap, or keep.
Feature Engineering
Categorical Features
Options: one-hot encoding, label encoding; show when to use which.
Numerical Features
Options: standard scaling, min–max scaling, robust scaling.
Date & Time Features
If datetime columns exist: extract year, month, day, weekday, etc.
Text Features (Optional)
If text columns present: mark them and suggest separate text preprocessing or basic cleaning (no need to implement full NLP).
Target Variable Processing
Let user select which column is the “target”.
For classification: handle label encoding.
For imbalanced classes: show class distribution + information about SMOTE/oversampling (you may add it as a future feature or simple toggle if easy).
Feature Selection (Basic)
Show correlation matrix for numerical features.
Let user optionally drop highly correlated features (above a threshold).
Allow dropping constant/low-variance features.
Train/Test Split
Let user choose test size (e.g., slider).
For classification: support stratified split.
For time-series (if datetime exists): show a note about time-based splitting and, if feasible, provide simple chronological split.
Export & Reproducibility
Allow user to:
Download the processed dataset as CSV.
See a summary of chosen preprocessing settings (like a preprocessing report).
Keep this simple but clear.
🧩 UX / UI REQUIREMENTS (VERY IMPORTANT)
This app should teach the user step-by-step while they preprocess. Update the UI accordingly:
Organize the preprocessing UI as a stepper / wizard or clearly separated sections in order:
1️⃣ Data Ingestion
2️⃣ Data Quality
3️⃣ Cleaning
4️⃣ Feature Engineering
5️⃣ Target & Imbalance
6️⃣ Feature Selection
7️⃣ Train/Test Split
8️⃣ Export
For each step, add:
A short title (e.g., “Step 3: Data Cleaning – Fix Missing Values & Outliers”).
A short paragraph:
What this step does.
Why it is important.
Why it comes after the previous step.
Use small info boxes (st.info, st.warning, etc.) to explain best practices.
Keep the design:
Clean and minimal.
Consistent spacing and headings.
Easy to follow from top to bottom like a guided flow.
Wherever a user chooses an option (e.g., imputation strategy, encoding type, scaling method), briefly explain:
When that option is preferred.
Possible trade-offs.
⚙️ IMPLEMENTATION GUIDELINES
Do NOT remove existing features unless they are clearly redundant or broken.
Prefer extending current modules instead of rewriting everything.
If large refactors are required:
First, organize code into clear functions for each preprocessing step.
Keep names descriptive (e.g., handle_missing_values, encode_categorical_features, etc.).
Avoid over-optimization; focus on clarity, modularity, and correctness.
Make sure all transformations are applied to a central DataFrame in a clear, traceable flow.
Ensure that the user can see intermediate results after major steps (e.g., cleaned data preview, encoded data preview).
✅ DELIVERABLES / WHAT I EXPECT YOU TO DO
Scan the current repo and identify:
Which preprocessing steps already exist.
Which are missing.
Update or create:
A main preprocessing page or flow that follows the step order above.
Helper functions for each step.
UI components that explain each step (what/why/why-after-previous).
Ensure:
The user can go through the entire pipeline from upload → export.
Each step feels like a mini-tutorial.
Existing workflows still work (no broken pages).
After changes:
Clean up unused code if any,
Keep everything readable and maintainable.
